To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the visual world paradigm is an excellent tool for exploring the time course of sentence processing (b) thematic information conveyed by a pre verbal argument in a head final language such as Japanese can be used to constrain the interpretation of an upcoming head and (c) the same is true of a pre verbal argument and an upcoming head in a head initial language such as English.

1) the visual world paradigm provides a useful tool for investigating the time course of incremental processing in sentence comprehension, and 2) incremental processing can be observed even when the linguistic input provides no information about the upcoming material.

(1) The time course of incremental sentence processing is not limited to the immediate processing of linguistic information, but includes the anticipation of upcoming linguistic material based on non linguistic information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how a sentence is understood in the moment, and how the understanding of one word is affected by the understanding of the words preceding it.
the nature of incremental processing, with its relation to the architecture of the language processor and with the extent to which it is constrained by linguistic and other factors.
the nature of the information that can be extracted from the linguistic input and how this information is used to anticipate the subsequent linguistic input.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

anticipatory eye movement is the hallmark of a processor that can draw on different sources, including non-linguistic information, at the earliest possible point in time, to establish the fullest and most appropriate interpretation possible at each moment in the processing of an utterance.
the time course of prediction of upcoming material is determined by a number of factors, including the type of construction, the type of dependency, the type of language, and the type of task.
anticipatory processes are not limited to syntactic constraints but are based on a variety of information sources, including lexical, semantic and pragmatic information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
incremental processing is a matter of incremental interpretation.

the human sentence processing mechanism has the ability to anticipate the next argument based not only on the information provided by a head verb, but also on the information provided in the pre verbal argument.
the visual world paradigm can be used as a powerful tool for investigating incremental sentence processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the incremental processor is a more sophisticated and flexible device than has been previously appreciated.

a full understanding of the incremental nature of sentence processing must take into account the fact that it can draw on a range of sources of information that can be extracted in advance of the linguistic input itself, and that the time course of processing can be influenced by such sources of information in advance of their linguistic expression.
the 'visual world paradigm' is ideally suited to exploring such incremental processing.
